user.title: HassStore Tunnel
user.description:
Publish this Home Assistant to the internet through HassStore. Generate an 8-digit **access code** (bind code) on the site first (User Center → Intranet Tunnel → Install Wizard). It is a one-time credential — **not** an SMS/email verification code; enter it once here and the binding completes permanently.

Please read the HassStore Tunnel Terms of Service before accepting. The main line is located outside mainland China; tunnel configuration, usage and access logs may be transferred to and stored outside the PRC (Article 10 / Appendix B — separate consent).

environment.title: Where should the data plane run?
environment.description:
This machine runs HAOS (Supervisor detected). Installing the tunnel client as an app is recommended: separate container, Supervisor watchdog self-healing, and the tunnel survives HA restarts. Tick the option below to run it inside Home Assistant Core instead (simpler, but the tunnel drops when HA restarts).

Note: the bind code is valid for 10 minutes and single-use — use Back to change the site URL or the code.

data.local_client: Run hs-frpc inside the integration (do not install the app)

binary.title: Verify the hs-frpc binary
binary.description:
The in-integration mode downloads and verifies hs-frpc. For security reasons the SHA256 must be provided first — otherwise the integration refuses to download or execute any binary.

The SHA256 for your architecture ({arch}) has been **auto-fetched from the site's release manifest**. If it was not fetched (the server has no release directory, or you self-host without published binaries), open {manifest_url} and paste the matching value manually.

data_description.binary_mirror: Official mirror by default (the mirror_base returned by {manifest_url}); use your own mirror for faster access.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-bind HassStore Tunnel
reauth_confirm.description: The device token is no longer valid (disabled, rotated, or the device was deleted on the site). Generate a new access code on the site (Intranet Tunnel → Install Wizard) and enter it below.

init.title: HassStore Tunnel options
init.description: Local target, transport protocol and log level. Changes reload the integration (and persist across restarts).

data.auto_update_app: Allow Supervisor to auto-update the app
data.local_client: Run inside the integration (do not install the app)

data_description.local_target: App mode always uses host `homeassistant`, in-integration mode uses `127.0.0.1`. **Leave empty to auto-follow Home Assistant's actual HTTP port** (recommended — since HA 2026.x, Core listens on port 80 under Supervisor, not 8123). A custom port must be in the site's origin whitelist (default 8123,80).
data_description.log_level: trace / debug / info / warning / error. Use debug temporarily when troubleshooting.
data_description.binary_sha256: Required for the in-integration data plane; leaving it empty refuses to download or run hs-frpc (secure default). Pre-filled for your architecture from the site's release manifest (/api/v1/tunnel/release/manifest). Maintained automatically when auto-update is on — normally no need to change it.
data_description.auto_update_client: When enabled, the integration compares the site's release manifest every 6 hours and, if a newer version exists, downloads it, verifies its SHA256, replaces the binary atomically and restarts the client (the tunnel drops for a few seconds). **Enabling this follows the site's published version**; to pin a specific build, turn it off and point the mirror at a host that serves that build (the official mirror only serves the latest) together with the matching `binary_sha256`. Only applies to the in-integration (local) data plane — in app mode the binary lives inside the container and is managed by `auto_update_app`.

binary_integrity.title: hs-frpc failed integrity verification — tunnel stopped

trusted_proxies.title: trusted_proxies must be configured, otherwise login loops forever
trusted_proxies.description:
The tunnel forwards visitor traffic to Home Assistant through the edge Nginx, so HA must treat those proxies as trusted. Otherwise every request appears to come from a proxy address and session validation fails — the symptom is «log in and get bounced back to the login page».

Add the following under `http:` in `/config/configuration.yaml`:

```yaml
http:
  use_x_forwarded_for: true
  trusted_proxies:
    - 172.30.32.0/23
    - 127.0.0.1
    - ::1
```

**Currently missing**: {missing}

Then restart Home Assistant. See the app's Documentation page for the proxy addresses of each line/edge.
